title: think session is a pure reducer + shell
rationale: Keeps UX logic testable without a terminal; one event per mutation

description: macOS fs.watch on a directory coalesces rename-over saves (vim style) and may report only the temp file name, not idea.md.
resolution: watch.ts re-reads on ANY directory event (content compare filters noise) plus a 1s poll fallback

name: live agent arrivals via reducer arrive input
description: think watches questions.jsonl (tier>=1) and dispatches {type:'arrive'} into the pure session reducer: arrivals go before the first unreached rule question (never ahead of the current one); a full queue bumps the last unreached rule question (stays open for next session) or leaves the arrival for next session. A 'seen' id set prevents re-queuing bumped/pre-existing questions.

name: nested-tui-handoff
description: tend hands an accepted split to a think session: the shell stops its Terminal, awaits an injected ThinkRunner (commands/think.ts startThink with ScreenGuidance), then restarts the Terminal with the same dispatch. Pure reducers (tend.ts, session.ts) never see the handoff; tests drive both on one fakeTerminal.
macOS FSEvents drops fs.watch events for a load-dependent window right after watch() returns; the pollMs:0 rename test in src/watch.test.ts failed ~1 in 10 runs under CPU load.
resolution: Tests rewrite the file until the watcher reports a change (armed() helper) instead of a fixed sleep; product code is covered by the 1s poll fallback.
